spec_role: Extends the landed tutorial flashcards from a single 7-card admin deck into a role-aware, two-level guided tour: every role gets a deck of its real modules first, then each module drills into its real sub-modules, with skip tour at every level, resume where left off, and a completion state. Grounds the tour in the actual route trees and route guards so no card can advertise a module that does not exist or a link the role cannot open.

north_star.destination_sentence: One real school, 500-2000 students, one board, one state, runs one full academic term entirely on SchoolMitra: zero Excel registers, zero untracked phone calls, fee cycle closed monthly, attendance under four minutes per section, exams conducted end to end with published results — and the school renews and refers another school.

target_metrics_moved.target: 95%+ of started journeys reach their finished state
target_metrics_moved.expected_delta: The tour itself becomes an instrumented journey with started / completed / skipped telemetry; first-session orientation stops being a dead end for the ten roles that currently have no tour at all

north_star.metric_rule: Tour events are plain usage events carrying journey id and role, first-party, tenant-isolated, zero PII. They are NOT north_star events; the six north-star event definitions in docs/product/metrics.md are untouched. A tour completion is not a business outcome and must never be presented as one.

intent: The first flashcard cut landed for one role only: seven module cards on the school admin dashboard, dismissed once via localStorage, no sub-modules, no skip progress, no completion state, and nothing for the other ten roles. The user's requirement is a real guided tour: modules first, then sub-modules, skippable at every level, for every role. The defect class this spec prevents is the series' recurring fabricated-truth class applied to tours: a card that describes a module that does not exist, links to a route the role cannot open, or claims progress that was not earned. The tour engine therefore derives its content from the codebase's real route trees, verifies every card target against the role's route guards in an automated test, and treats the route tree as the single source of truth for what the tour may claim. The tour is part of J10: a school where the office admin, teachers, accountant, and principal each finish their first session knowing where their jobs live is a school that reaches Day One readiness faster and stays.

non_goals_confirmed: No hardware, no edtech content, no LLMs in workflows, no new role apps, no price tiers, no WhatsApp
out_of_scope_for_this_spec: Changing the six north-star metric definitions or their emission; tour telemetry is plain usage events
Changing onboarding wizard steps or the unified super-admin provisioning flow landed in a0d5b9fb beyond mounting the super-admin deck
Video tutorials, tooltips-on-page, or spotlight overlays; this spec is flashcard decks only
Multi-language tour copy; English first, i18n later
Server-side tour progress sync; localStorage per role is the accepted store for now

tour_laws.law_1_route_truth: Every card's ctaHref must be a real route in the role's app directory and must pass that role's assertRouteAccess guard. An automated test walks every deck and fails the build on a dead or forbidden link. The route tree is the single source of truth for what a deck may claim.
tour_laws.law_2_no_fabricated_modules: A deck contains only modules that exist in the code. A thin role gets a short deck. Padding with invented modules is the fabricated-truth defect class and is prohibited.
tour_laws.law_3_two_levels: Level 1 is modules. Level 2 is the chosen module's real sub-modules. Navigation: module card offers 'See what's inside' to drill down, a breadcrumb returns to module level, and the level indicator always shows where the user is (Module 3 of 7 / Sub-module 2 of 5).
tour_laws.law_4_skip_everywhere: A 'Skip tour' control is visible at every level and every card. Skipping ends the tour and marks it dismissed for that role. A 'Skip this module' control at module level jumps to the next module without forcing its sub-modules.
tour_laws.law_5_resume_and_complete: Progress (current level, current module, current sub-module) persists per role in localStorage. Returning resumes where the user left, unless the tour was completed or dismissed. Reaching the last card renders a completion state with a 'Restart tour' action and the launcher button remains permanently available in the role's home header.
tour_laws.law_6_job_named_cards: Every card's title names the job the surface does (charter BR1), its summary is one sentence a tired adult reads in five seconds, and 'what it is / why it matters' stays honest to what the surface actually does in code. Card copy is written from the L0 audit of the real pages, not from imagination.
tour_laws.law_7_one_engine: One tour engine, one card schema, per-role deck definitions as data. No per-role copies of the component. The existing FeatureTutorialFlashCards shell is refactored into this engine, not forked.

business_logic_rules: BR-RT-1: The route tree plus route guards are the single source of truth for deck content. A card without a verified, role-accessible ctaHref does not ship (law_1).
BR-RT-2: One engine, per-role deck data. Duplicated per-role components do not merge (law_7).
BR-RT-3: Skip tour is visible at every level and every card; skip persists as dismissed for that role; the launcher button always allows revisit (law_4).
BR-RT-4: Progress persists per role and resumes; completion is a real state with restart; a dismissed tour never auto-opens again (law_5).
BR-RT-5: Tour telemetry is first-party usage events with role and journey id, tenant-scoped, zero PII; north-star metric definitions remain untouched.
BR-RT-6: Card copy is honest to the code: a module that cannot do X must not say it does X (charter BR2/BR3 spirit; the honesty scanners' law applied to tour content).
BR-RT-7: Decks render and are skippable on mobile viewports and in offline states where the host PWA supports offline.
BR-RT-8: Security unchanged: assertRouteAccess remains the authorization authority; the tour adds no routes, no new permissions, and no data access.
acceptance_criteria: AC-RT-1: docs/product/tour-card-matrix.md exists, covers all eleven roles, and every ctaHref in it resolves to a real page file.
AC-RT-2: The tour engine supports module level, sub-module drill-down, breadcrumb back, level indicator, skip tour, skip module, resume, completion, and restart, all covered by automated state tests.
AC-RT-3: The admin deck shows the real admin modules with sub-modules and mounts on both the dashboard and the Day One Cockpit with launcher buttons in both headers.
AC-RT-4: Teacher, principal, accountant, hr-manager, librarian, transport-manager, and driver each have a deck mounted on their home surface, sized honestly to their real surfaces.
AC-RT-5: Parent and student decks exist, speak family language, work on mobile and offline where the host PWA does, and never reference admin surfaces.
AC-RT-6: The super-admin deck exists and the unified provisioning completion view points the operator at the new school's tour without changing sessions.
AC-RT-7: The route-truth test passes in CI for every deck and demonstrably fails on a dead or forbidden link.
AC-RT-8: tour_started, tour_completed, and tour_skipped are emitted tenant-scoped with role and journey id, and no north_star event definition changed.
AC-RT-9: Skip, resume, and completion behave per the laws on every role: refresh resumes an in-progress tour, dismissed tours stay dismissed, launcher reopens at the saved position.
AC-RT-10: Keyboard navigation, focus management, and reduced motion pass; all eleven decks render on mobile and desktop viewports.
AC-RT-11: journey-map.md J10 row records the tour as a completed onboarding surface with evidence; page-level gaps found during L0 are recorded as gap entries.
AC-RT-12: Typecheck, build, and smoke render green; zero new npm dependencies; the existing FeatureTutorialFlashCards usages are migrated, not left dangling.
constraints: Zero new npm dependencies. The engine is a refactor of the existing component shell.
Phases land in strict order RT-L0 through RT-L7, one commit series per layer. Commit prefixes: docs(tour) for L0, feat(tour) for L1 through L7.
Every phase lands with typecheck, build, and smoke render green. The S7 gate is permanent series law.
The L0 matrix is a review artifact: the operator approves the card matrix before decks are authored in L2 through L5.
Do not modify north-star metric definitions, the onboarding wizard's steps, or the unified provisioning flow beyond the L5 handoff text.
Do not add tooltip, spotlight, or video tour mechanisms; flashcard decks only.
Where this spec conflicts with in-repo security constraints, security wins; log the conflict in the commit body.

Deck data lives in one location per the repo's conventions (suggested: frontend/src/lib/tours/ or frontend/src/components/onboarding/tours/); follow the codebase's existing structure at implementation time.
definition_of_done: The tour is done when every one of the eleven roles, on first login on the demo tenant, can take a two-level guided tour of their real modules and sub-modules, skip it at any point, refresh and resume, finish it and restart it, and when every link on every card of every deck opens under that role's own route guard, enforced by a CI test. The tour is instrumented with first-party usage events, the north-star definitions are untouched, and journey-map.md records J10's onboarding surface as complete with per-role evidence. A new employee at a customer school learns the product in their first session without calling anyone.
